blocks.x: 1.0 Institutional Framework

This Regulation, issued pursuant to the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended), applies to the investment, custody, and management of all pension fund assets under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), including:
Retirement Savings Accounts (RSAs) administered by Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs);
Pension funds managed under Approved Existing Schemes (AES);
Pension funds administered by Closed Pension Fund Administrators (CPFAs).

In the event of any inconsistency between the provisions of this Regulation and other investment guidelines previously issued by the Commission, the provisions of this Regulation shall prevail to the extent of such inconsistency, without prejudice to the overriding provisions of the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended).

Pension Fund Custodians (PFCs) shall only act on written instructions, including authenticated electronic instructions, from PFAs in respect of the investment and management of pension fund assets held in their custody. Such instructions shall be in accordance with the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended) and relevant Commission guidelines.

In discharging their contractual functions to PFAs, the PFCs shall not contract out the custody of pension fund assets to third parties, except for allowable investments made outside Nigeria. The PFC shall obtain prior approval from the Commission before engaging a global Custodian for such allowable foreign investments.

The PFAs shall not contract out the investment or management of pension fund assets to third parties in the discharge of their contractual obligations to Contributors, except as expressly permitted under the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended), this Regulation, or any subsequent circulars or guidelines issued by the Commission. In all such cases, the PFA shall retain ultimate fiduciary responsibility and oversight for the assets.
The PFAs shall maintain a Multi-Fund Structure as provided in this Regulation, to govern the investment of pension fund assets of RSA Funds.

In addition to the requirements of other guidelines issued by the Commission on corporate governance, ethics and business practices, each PFA shall establish an Investment Strategy Committee as well as a Risk Management Committee, in compliance with Section 78 of the Pension Reform Act, 2014 ("the Act" or "PRA 2014").

The Investment Strategy Committee, in addition to other functions specified in the Act, shall formulate internal investment strategies to enable compliance with this Regulation, taking into cognizance the macro-economic environment as well as the investment objectives and risk profile of the respective Funds. The internal investment strategies shall be approved by the PFA in a formal Board Meeting at least once every year or as frequently as changes occur in the macroeconomic environment that may affect pension fund assets.

The Risk Management Committee shall determine the acceptable risk profile of each investment portfolio, draw up risk assessment and measurement systems, monitor their portfolio against risk tolerance limits, as well as all other functions relating to risk management specified in the PRA 2014 and as may be determined by the PFA's Board and the Commission, from time to time. The Risk Management Committee shall render a report of its activities to the PFA's Board and the Commission at least once every quarter.

Each of the Committees in Sections 1.6 and 1.7 above shall have at least one Non-Executive Director with relevant skills and experience as a member. In addition, an Independent Director shall chair the Risk Management Committee.
The Commission shall provide the necessary guidelines on the investment of Pension Fund Assets outside the territory of the Federal Republic of Nigeria as and when the need arises.
2.0 Definition of Terms

AAIOFI: The Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI) is an Islamic international autonomous not-for-profit corporate body that prepares accounting, auditing, governance, ethics and Shari'ah standards for Islamic financial institutions and the industry.
Alternative Investments: Asset classes and investment vehicles that fall outside the scope of traditional investments, such as Private Equity, Infrastructure Fund, REITS, etc.

Asset-Backed Securities (ABS): Certificates, whether written or electronic, issued by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), the repayment of which shall be derived from the cash flow of the pool of assets, in accordance with the terms and conditions of the transaction. Assets used in the term Asset-backed securities refer to loans receivable or other similar financial assets with an expected cash payment stream, e.g. receivables, mortgage loans, leases, etc.
Bank: A commercial or merchant bank licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).
Central Securities Depository: Is an institution integrated with an Exchange to clear and settle transactions traded on an Exchange and act as a depository for certificates of investments.
Commission: National Pension Commission, established under the Pension Reform Act (PRA) 2014.

Commodities: Any produce, item, commodity, article, index, right, or interest of any nature as defined in the Investment and Securities Act (ISA) 2025, subject to guidelines issued by the Commission from time to time.
Conventional or Non-Shari'ah Compliant instruments: Refers to Financial securities that do not comply with Shari'ah principles and are not sanctioned by
the Financial Regulatory Advisory Council of Experts.
CPFA: Closed Pension Fund Administrator licensed by the Commission.

Depositary Notes (DN): Debt instrument issued by a depositary bank. The notes representing ownership of bonds denominated in a local currency held in custody in the same jurisdiction where the underlying bonds are traded.
Depositary Receipts (DR): Negotiable financial instrument issued by a depositary bank. It represents shares in a foreign company and trades on the local stock exchanges in the investor's country.

Eligible Instruments: Categories of financial assets and investment vehicles approved by the Commission into which Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) may invest pension fund assets, in accordance with the provisions of the Pension Reform Act 2014 and the Regulation on Investment of Pension Fund Assets.

Eligible States and Local Governments or Eligible Listed or Unlisted Corporate Entities: entities that are fully implementing the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), as confirmed by the Commission on its website.

Exchange Traded Fund (ETF): A unit trust scheme or an open-ended investment company that issues unleveraged securities or units listed on a securities exchange recognized or registered by the Securities & Exchange Commission (SEC) in Nigeria and tracks the performance of specified securities or assets, which includes but is not limited to equities, basket of assets, indices, commodity prices, foreign currency rates or any other appropriate benchmark approved by SEC from time to time subject to guidelines issued by the Commission.

Financial Regulatory Advisory Council of Experts (FRACE): Is an advisory body on Islamic Banking and Finance established by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to advise on matters relating to the Islamic commercial jurisprudence for the effective regulation and supervision of Non-Interest Financial Institutions
and products in Nigeria.
Forward Rate Agreement (FRA): A derivative contract between two parties to lock in an agreed interest rate to be applied on a principal amount for a specified future period.
Gharar: Any commercial transaction associated with uncertainty, deception and excessive speculation "the sale of what is not yet present", such as crops not yet harvested or fish not yet netted.

Licensed Pension Fund Operators (LPFOs): Entities that have been duly authorized by the Commission to carry out specific functions within Nigeria's pension industry, in line with the provisions of the PRA 2014.

Margin Account: An account maintained with a lender, either a bank or broker, which records the buying and selling of securities by the bank or broker, for themselves or their clients, through loans or credits.

Market Participants: Market participants are individuals or entities that actively engage in a market, whether it's buying, selling, or facilitating transactions. They can be individuals, businesses, or institutions involved in various activities, such as trading, investing, or providing goods and services within a specific market.

Mortgage-Backed Securities (MBS): MBS are Securities whose repayments shall be derived from the cash flows of real estate or real estate-related assets in accordance with the terms and conditions of the transaction.

Mudarabah: Is a form of Islamic equity-based partnership contract, commonly known as a profit-sharing contract. It is a profit-sharing and loss-bearing partnership contract where the capital provider contributes the capital while the manager provides managerial skills to manage the mudarabah accordingly.
Multilateral Development Finance Organizations (MDFOs): Organizations

formed between three or more nations to work on development issues related to all the countries in the respective organizations e.g. World Bank Group, African Finance Corporation, and African Development Bank. The Federal Ministry of Finance shall approve such eligible MDFOs.

Non-Interest compliant instruments: Financial securities and specialist investment funds that comply with the provisions of Islamic Commercial Jurisprudence (Shari'ah) and any other established non- interest principles, as approved by the Advisory Council of Experts or any other body constituted by the SEC and/or CBN or jointly by the two institutions.
Options: A Contractual agreement that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined price on or before a specified date.
Pension Fund Assets: Pension assets under management and custody of Licensed Pension Operators.
PFA: Pension Fund Administrator licensed by the Commission to manage pension funds and assets.

PFC: A Pension Fund Custodian licensed by the Commission for the sole purpose of keeping custody of pension funds and assets in trust for employees, as well as beneficiaries of the RSA and other retirement benefit schemes.

PRA 2014: The Pension Reform Act 2014 is the Act that repeals the Pension Reform Act no.2, 2004 and enacts the Pension Reform Act 2014 to continue to govern and regulate the administration of the uniform contributory pension scheme for both the public and private sectors in Nigeria.
Primary Market: A market by which companies can raise fresh capital by issuing securities (e.g. shares and debentures, etc.) to the investing public.
Private and Public Companies: In line with Sections 22 and 24 of the

Company and Allied Matters Act 2020, and without prejudice to other provisions of the definitions, a private company shall be so designated in its Memorandum of Association and shall have a total number of members not exceeding 50 persons. Any company other than a private company shall be a public company and its memorandum shall state that it is a public company.

Private Equity Fund: Any designated pool of investment capital targeted at all stages of private equity investment from start-ups to large buy-outs, including those held by corporate entities, limited partnerships and other investment vehicles, including Fund of Funds.

Ratings: The evaluation of the credit risk of an instrument in case of debt, a bank for deposit placements and a company with respect to guarantees. A credit rating of "A-" or "A+" is considered to be an "A" rating under this Regulation. Similarly, a credit rating of "BBB- "or "BBB+" is considered to be a "BBB" rating. Please refer to the mapping in Appendix 1.

Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs): Company or Trust Scheme that owns, operates, or finances income-generating real estate and allows investors to pool funds to invest in property-related assets without directly owning or managing the properties.

Related Persons or Related Parties: Natural persons related by blood, adoption or marriage; legal entities, one of which has control or significant influence over the other, or both of which are controlled by some other person or entity; a corporate entity where any of the aforementioned holds 5% or more beneficial interest; and any other relationship that can be reasonably construed as related persons or parties.

REPO: Repurchase/ Reverse Repurchase Agreement (REPO) is a contractual arrangement between two parties, where one party agrees to sell securities to another party at a specified price with a commitment to buy the securities back at a later date.

Safekeeping Receipts: A document issued by a financial institution (like a bank or brokerage firm) acknowledging that it is holding an asset on behalf of another party. It serves as a confirmation that the asset is being stored securely and that the institution is responsible for its safekeeping.
Secondary Market: A market, where securities initially issued in the primary market are bought and sold.
2.39 Securities include:
Debentures, stocks, bonds or Sukuk issued or proposed to be issued by a government;
Debentures, shares, bonds, Sukuk, or notes issued or proposed to be issued by a body corporate;
Any right or option in respect of any such debentures, stocks, Shares, bonds, Sukuk, or notes; and

Commodities futures, contracts, options and other derivatives, and the term securities include those securities in the category of the securities listed in (a) - (c) above which may be transferred by means of any electronic mode approved by SEC and which may be deposited, kept or stored with any licensed depository or custodian company as provided under the ISA 2025.
Securities Exchange: Means an exchange or an approved trading facility (Composite or Non-composite) as defined in the ISA 2025.

State/Local Governments: Means all the State and Local Governments of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, including the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) and Area Councils in the FCT, which are listed in the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).
Sukuk: Refers to investment certificates or notes of equal value which evidences undivided interest/ownership of tangible assets, usufructs and
services or 351 SEC Rules; June 2013 investment in the assets of particular projects or special investment activity using Shari'ah principles and concepts approved by the SEC.

Supra-national Bonds or Supranational Sukuk: Means Debt instruments issued by Multilateral Development Finance Organizations, of which Nigeria is a member and its membership approved by the Federal Ministry of Finance.
Swaps: Financial derivative contract in which two parties agree to exchange (or "swap") sets of cash flows or financial obligations over a specified period, based on predetermined terms.

Wakala Bil-Istithmar: Is an Islamic agency contract whereby Islamic financial institutions manage funds on behalf of their customers. This involves providing agency (wakala) charges against specific fund management fees.

Private and Public Companies: In line with Sections 22 and 24 of the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, and without prejudice to other provisions of the definitions, a private company shall be so designated in its Memorandum of Association and shall have a total number of members not exceeding 50 persons. Any company other than a private company shall be a public company, and its memorandum shall state that it is a public company.
3.0 General Principles
PFAs shall invest pension fund assets with the objectives of safety and the maintenance of fair returns.
An instrument or institution seeking pension fund investment shall be rated by at least two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating agency incorporated in Nigeria and registered with the SEC.

In the event of rating agencies giving different rating grades on a particular instrument, issue, or issuer, the lower rating grade obtainable in the market shall apply to determine the relevant maximum investment limit.
By virtue of Section 10 (2) of the PRA 2014, all interests, dividends, profits, and other incomes accruable to pension funds and assets shall not be taxable.
PFAs shall recruit and retain personnel with relevant skills in the Investment Department.

PFAs shall not invest Pension Fund Assets in instruments that are subject to any type of prohibition or limitation on the sale or purchase of such instrument, except for open/close-end/hybrid funds and specialist investment funds allowed by this Regulation.
PFAs shall not trade on margin accounts with pension fund assets.
PFAs shall not engage in borrowing or lending of pension fund assets except under the Securities Lending Arrangement or Repurchase Agreements (REPOs) guidelines issued by the Commission.
PFAs shall not trade in financial instruments with pension fund assets at prices that are prejudicial to the pension fund assets.

Pension fund assets shall only be invested in bonds, Sukuk, or other debt instruments issued by eligible MDFOs, State/Local Governments, and Corporate Entities that are fully implementing the Contributory Pension Scheme. The Commission shall publish on its website, from time to time, the lists of compliant State/Local Governments and Corporate Entities.
Pension fund assets shall only be invested in bonds, Sukuk or other debt instruments of MDFOs and SPV that are implementing a pension arrangement approved by the Commission.
Notwithstanding the provision of 3.10 and 3.11 above, evidence of pension contribution remittance under the Contributory Pension Scheme may not be required where:
i. The MDFO has an existing pension arrangement for its personnel.
ii. The SPV is a non-operating or Project SPV whose sponsor complies with the requirements of the Contributory Pension Scheme.
PFAs are to ensure that appropriate legal and financial due diligence are undertaken on all Prospectus/Offer Documents of all allowable instruments prior to investment.
Pursuant to 3.13 above, PFAs shall take into consideration the following amongst others, in corporate entities or specialist investment funds in which pension fund assets are to be invested:
i. Rules governing the Board of the corporate entity or Fund;
ii. Continuous disclosure rules of material events in the corporate entity or Fund; and

iii. Adequate disclosures of the financial condition of the corporate entity or Fund, in the annual financial statements, which shall be audited by an independent firm of chartered accountants registered with the Financial Reporting Council (FRC).

PFAs/CPFAs shall incorporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors into their investment decision-making processes, emphasizing governance and responsible investing, encouraging collaboration and inclusive growth, and allocating long-term assets to priority sectors that promote sustainable national development or other thematic areas as designated by the Commission.
4.0 Authorized Markets
Primary and Secondary market transactions shall be carried out on exchanges approved in line with the provisions of the ISA 2025.

All primary market investments by PFAs in ordinary or preference shares of eligible corporate entities shall only be through public offerings, listing by introduction or private placement approved by the SEC.
All secondary market trading of pension assets, shall occur on securities exchanges or trading platforms recognized by the SEC.

All primary market investments by PFAs in bonds, Sukuk, debenture and other debt instruments issued by eligible corporate entities shall be through public offering or private placement arrangements approved by SEC. PFAs may invest in bonds or Sukuk issued by publicly listed companies through private placement arrangements provided they fulfill the requirements in Section 6.2.4 of this Regulation.

All primary market investments by PFAs in participation units of Open, CloseEnd, Hybrid Investment Funds, including ETFs, Specialist Investment Funds (REITs, Infrastructure Fund and Private Equity Fund) and other Non-interest compliant instruments shall be through public offering or private placement arrangements, except when:

i. Trading with participation units of Open/Closed-end or Hybrid Investment Funds on the memorandum list of a securities exchange registered by the SEC or Specialist Investment Funds (Infrastructure and Private Equity) and
Non-Interest (Shari'ah) Compliant Investment Funds registered by SEC.
ii. Acquiring or trading in securities of an eligible Nigerian corporate entity, listed or quoted in an Offshore Securities Exchange.
5.0 Allowable Instruments
Pension fund assets shall be invested in the following allowable instruments:

Bonds, Sukuk, Treasury Bills, Depository Receipts, Promissory Notes and other securities issued by the Federal Government of Nigeria and CBN or their agencies as well as Special Purpose Vehicles and Companies created/owned by the Federal Government of Nigeria, provided that the Federal Government of Nigeria or the CBN guarantees the securities.

Bonds and Sukuk issued by eligible State and Local Governments or State Government Agencies or wholly owned companies of the State Government, or any other arrangement of which a State or Local Government is the ultimate beneficiary, provided that such securities are fully guaranteed by Irrevocable Standing Payment Orders (ISPOs) against State's Federal Allocation or external guarantees by MDFOs with a minimum credit rating of 'AA'.

Sukuk, debentures, redeemable/ convertible preference shares, and other debt instruments issued by public and private corporate entities, Asset-Backed Securities including Mortgage Bonds, Mortgage-Backed Securities, and Infrastructure Bonds / Sukuk.

Debt securities issued by corporate entities and guaranteed by the Federal/State Governments, MDFOs, or any agency backed by a sovereign or Development Finance Institution with a minimum credit rating of AA.

Eligible agricultural sector instruments, such as debt securities, equities, and infrastructure projects within the agricultural value chain, provided such instruments meet the eligibility, quality, valuation, and risk management requirements specified under the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended), and this Regulation.
Non-interest compliant instruments including:
i. Government Sukuk (including Islamic Treasury Bills and Euro Sukuk) issued by FGN, CBN or FGN Agencies and Infrastructure Sukuk, backed by FGN/CBN guarantee.
ii. Corporate Sukuk (including Shari'ah-compliant ABS, MBS, DNs, Euro Sukuk & Infrastructures Sukuk), Supranational Sukuk.
iii. Shari'ah-compliant Money Market instruments.
iv. Shari'ah-compliant ordinary shares (including DRs)
v. Shari'ah-compliant infrastructure funds, Shari'ah-compliant private equity Funds, Shari'ah-compliant Open/Closed/Hybrid Funds and Shari'ahcompliant real Estate funds.

Ordinary Shares of Public Limited Liability Companies whether listed, unlisted or proposed to be listed through public offering, listing by introduction or private placement on a Securities Exchange registered by SEC.
Money Market Instruments of Banks and Commercial Papers issued by eligible corporate entities.
Open/ Close-ended/ Hybrid Investment Funds, including Exchange Traded Funds (ETF), Gold Backed ETF and Non-Interest Compliant Investment Funds, registered with the SEC.
Specialist Investment Funds whose underlying assets are tangible physical assets. These include:
i. Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) registered by SEC.
ii. Private Equity Funds registered with SEC.
iii. Infrastructure Funds registered with SEC.
iv. Exchange Traded Derivatives.
Supranational Bonds and Supranational Sukuk issued by eligible MDFOs approved by the Federal Ministry of Finance.

DRs/Ns and Eurobonds issued by eligible Nigerian corporate entities as well as Naira-denominated Depository Receipts/Notes issued locally and listed on a securities exchange that is a member of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE).
SKRs tradable on an Exchange recognized by the SEC.
6.0 Quality Requirements for Allowable Instruments
6.1 Rating Requirements
The following rating requirements shall apply:
All ratings shall be undertaken by rating agencies incorporated in Nigeria and registered with the SEC or foreign rating agencies recognized by the SEC.

Bonds and Sukuks issued by States, Local Governments, and Corporate Entities as well as Infrastructure Bonds and other allowable debt instruments in which pension fund assets are to be invested, shall have a minimum credit rating of 'A' issued by, at least, two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating agency incorporated in Nigeria and registered with SEC.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 6.1.2, PFAs may invest a maximum of 20% of pension assets under management in any combination of debt instruments issued by States, Local Governments, and Corporate Entities, with a credit rating of 'BBB' issued by, at least, two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating agency incorporated in Nigeria and registered with SEC.

The money market instruments of any bank shall have a minimum credit rating of 'BBB' issued by at least two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating agency incorporated in Nigeria and registered with SEC to qualify for investment of pension funds.

For Commercial Papers (CPs), pension fund assets shall only be invested in CPs of Corporate Entities with a minimum credit rating of 'A' issued by at least two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating agency incorporated in Nigeria. However, the CPs of 'BBB' rated corporate entities can be considered for investment, if guaranteed by any agency backed by a sovereign or Development Finance Institution with a minimum credit rating of AA.

Any Eurobond issued by an eligible Nigerian Corporate Entity in which pension fund assets are to be invested shall have a credit rating not lower than the sovereign rating of Nigeria at the time of issuance by a SEC recognized rating agency.

Bond, Sukuk, and other allowable debt instruments issued by eligible MDFOs in which pension fund assets are to be invested shall have a minimum credit rating of 'BBB' issued by a SEC recognized rating agency.
The minimum rating specified above shall be maintained throughout the tenor of the investments.
At the expiration of the specified ratings above, the pension fund may retain such investment for a maximum of 6 months after the expiration.

If at any time an existing investment is no longer authorized as a result of a credit rating downgrade, resulting in a new rating that is not more than one grade below the stipulated minimum, the pension fund may retain such investment to maturity.

If at any time an existing investment is no longer authorized, as a result of either a credit rating withdrawal or a credit rating downgrade by more than one grade or for any other reason, the PFA shall forward its exit strategy to the Commission within 10 working days.
PFAs shall not rely only on ratings assigned by Rating Companies, as they are only complementary to PFAs' internal due diligence and analysis before investing in any instrument or issuer.
6.2 Other Quality Requirements
6.2.1 Requirements for Bonds Issued by MDFOs
Pension Fund Assets can only be invested in Bonds or Sukuks issued by MDFOs if:
i. The bonds/debt instruments meet the rating requirements in Section 6.1.
ii. The MDFO is recognized by FMOF.
iii. A minimum of 20% of the proceeds is utilized for projects within Nigeria.
iv. The amount on issue shall not be less than N20 billion.
6.2.2 Requirements for DRs/Ns
Pension Fund Assets may be invested in Depositary Receipts/Notes (DRs/Ns),
Eurobonds and Naira-denominated Depository Receipts/Notes. However, the following minimum qualifying requirements shall apply:
i. DN and Eurobond instruments issued and guaranteed by the Federal Government of Nigeria shall be eligible for pension fund investments.

ii. Issuers of eligible DRs, DNs and Eurobonds, which are eligible Nigerian corporate entities, shall be registered and operating in Nigeria, as evidenced by current relevant tax filings and other regulatory filings with the Corporate Affairs Commission and any requisite supervisory regulatory agencies.

iii. In situations where off-shore subsidiaries are the issuing entities of the DNs and Eurobonds, they shall be wholly owned subsidiaries with the full obligations of the borrowing underwritten by their parent companies who shall be Nigerian corporate entities which are registered and operating in Nigeria, as evidenced by current relevant tax filings and other regulatory filings with the Corporate Affairs Commission and any relevant supervisory regulatory agencies.
iv. To qualify as an eligible instrument for investment by PFAs, the DR, DN or Eurobond issuances shall obtain necessary regulatory approvals from the country where the instruments are to be issued.
v. Where the instrument is a Naira-denominated Depository Receipt / Note, issued in Nigeria (sponsored and unsponsored) it shall meet the following conditions:
a. Shall be approved by SEC.
b. Shall be tradable on a SEC approved exchange.
vi. For unsponsored Depository Receipts/Notes:
a. The Arranger shall be licensed by SEC and the DR/N listed on a SEC recognized exchange.
b. The Depository shall provide evidence of possession of the instrument in the country of origin with a designated custodian approved by relevant authority to carry such a business.

The following maximum investment limits shall apply:
i. Portfolio Limit: PFA's total investment in all issued DRs, DNs, Nairadenominated DRs/DNs and Eurobonds shall not be more than 10% of the portfolio value of the pension fund in the RSA Fund.
ii. Per Issuer Limit: A maximum of 5% of pension fund assets under management may be invested in all DRs, DNs, Naira-denominated
DRs/DNs and Eurobonds issued by any one corporate entity or an arranger.
iii. Per Issue Limit: Pension fund assets may be invested in the DRs, DNs, Naira-denominated DRs/DNs and Eurobonds issued by any corporate entity, subject to a maximum limit of 2.5% of each issue.
The following settlement and custody arrangements shall apply, subject to prior approval by the Commission before execution:

i. PFCs may be required to establish accounts with any licensed central securities depository or any offshore clearing platform, regulated in its home jurisdiction, to provide settlement and custody services, to ensure the ability to provide a comprehensive and robust settlement platform for PFA transactions in DRs, DNs and Eurobonds.

ii. The accounts opened with such licensed securities depositories shall operate in a manner similar to the structure used by licensed central securities depositories for domestic securities transactions in Nigeria, whereby each PFC will maintain sub-accounts for each PFA and will hold and trade all securities related to each PFA from their respective subaccounts.

iii. Alternatively, PFCs can enter into settlement and sub-custody arrangements with Trustee/Nominee Companies in Nigeria that are registered with SEC and have a professional arrangement with a global Custodian Bank or members of licensed international securities depositories.

PFAs should refer to the CBN Foreign Exchange Guidelines from time to time on how to convert their Naira investment funds into the requisite foreign currency amount, which they will require to effect an investment in DRs, DNs, or Eurobonds.
6.2.3 Requirements for Corporate Debt Instruments

Pension Fund Assets can be invested in bonds, sukuks, debentures, redeemable/convertible preference shares, and other debt instruments issued by corporate entities, subject to the following conditions:
i. Approved by SEC.
ii. They have been duly issued.
iii. They meet the rating requirements in Section 6.1.
iv. They have clearly defined term/maturity features, periodic and terminal payout.
v. Where such securities have any embedded options e.g. call option, put option etc, they shall be clearly stated in the offer document/prospectus.
vi. The securities are to be listed on a securities exchange registered by SEC.
6.2.3.2 Private Issuance by Registered Corporate Entities

Pension Fund Assets can be invested in bonds, sukuks, debentures, redeemable/convertible preference shares and other debt instruments privately issued by Public and Private corporate entities, subject to the following:
i. They meet the rating requirements in Section 6.1.
ii. They have clearly defined term/maturity features, periodic and terminal payout.
iii. Where such securities have any embedded options, e.g. call options, put options, etc., they shall be clearly stated in the offer document/prospectus.
iv. The securities are to be noted on a securities exchange or trading platform recognized by SEC.

v. PFAs may invest in privately issued corporate bonds and sukuk, provided the principal and interest are guaranteed up to a minimum of 70% by MDFOs, any agency with a minimum credit rating of "AA" backed by a Sovereign, or a reputable financial institution with a minimum credit rating of "AA".
vi. Where the private issuance is by a Public Company, the eligible security shall be approved by SEC.
6.2.4 Requirements for Infrastructure Projects
6.2.4.1 Infrastructure Bonds/Sukuk
Pension Fund Assets can only be invested in infrastructure projects through eligible bonds, Sukuk, subject to the following requirements:
i. Any infrastructure project to be invested in, shall be:
Minimum of N10 billion in value.
Core infrastructure projects, whose business plans and financial projections indicate that they are financially viable.
ii. The bond or sukuk instrument issued to finance the infrastructure project shall, in addition to the requirements above, have:
Minimum credit rating of 'BBB',
Credit guarantees by the Federal Government of Nigeria, eligible MDFOs or any agency with a minimum credit rating of "AA" backed by a Sovereign or Development Finance Institution;
Maturity date that precedes the expiration of the concession, where applicable; and
Feasible and enforceable redemption procedure in the event of any adverse event that makes the project differ significantly from its original financial projections.
6.2.4.2 Infrastructure Fund
Where infrastructure projects are financed through Infrastructure Funds, pension fund investments shall be subject to the following requirements:
The value of the Infrastructure Fund shall not be less than N20 billion.
The Infrastructure Fund shall have well-defined and publicized investment objectives and strategy as well as disclosures of pricing of underlying assets, including any other necessary information.
All annual financial statements of the Fund shall be audited by independent
firm(s) of chartered accountants registered by the Financial Reporting Council (FRC).
The Infrastructure Fund shall have satisfactory pre-defined liquidity/exit routes such as IPO, sale to other Infrastructure Funds, Trade sale, sale to a strategic investor, etc.
The Funds shall be managed by experienced Fund Managers, versed in infrastructure financing and registered with the SEC as Fund Managers.
A minimum of 50% of the Infrastructure Fund shall be invested in projects within Nigeria.

The key Principals, namely the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Investment Officer (CIO), of the Fund Manager, shall each have at least ten (10) years of relevant and continuous experience in infrastructure financing or investment management.

The key Principals shall not exit the Fund without prior notice to the PFAs, which shall not be less than 90 days from the exit date. This 'exit clause' shall be expressly stated as a condition in the investment agreement/ covenant between the PFA and the Fund Manager.

Where an Infrastructure Fund does not have an eligible Sovereign Wealth Fund and/or MDFO as Limited Partners but the Fund Manager has a minimum Investment Manager Rating of 'BBB' issued by, at least, two rating agencies registered or recognized by SEC, the Fund Manager shall retain a minimum investment of 3% of the Infrastructure Fund.

Where the Infrastructure Fund has an eligible Sovereign Wealth Fund and/or Multilateral Development Finance Organization as Limited Partners, the Fund Manager shall retain a minimum of 1% of the Infrastructure Fund.
The Fund shall have an Advisory Board with independent representatives of Limited Partners, being in majority.
Prior to investment as well as during the tenor of investment in any

Infrastructure Fund, the Advisory Board in k above, shall have responsibility over audit functions regarding transactions with parties related to the Fund and compliance with the Fund's investment guidelines and policies.
6.2.4.3 Public Private Partnership

Where the infrastructure project is financed through Public Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement, the project shall be awarded to a concessionaire with a good track record, in accordance with the due process requirements set out in the Infrastructure Concession and Regulatory Commission Act (ICRC Act) and/ or any regulation made pursuant thereto and certified by the Infrastructure Concession and Regulatory Commission (ICRC) and approved by the Federal Executive Council (FEC).
6.2.5 Requirements for Investment in Real Estate

i. Pension Fund assets of RSA Funds under management with PFAs shall not directly invest in Real Estate, as investments shall only be through instruments such as Mortgage Backed Securities (MBS), Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITS) and similar Non-Interest Compliant Instruments.

ii. Notwithstanding (i) above, CPFAs and Approved Existing Schemes that operate Defined Benefit Schemes are allowed to directly invest in Real Estate, subject to Guidelines issued by the Commission from time to time.
6.2.5.1 Mortgage Backed Securities (MBS)
In the case of MBS, the following requirements shall apply:
i. Compliance with the rating requirements in Section 6.1.
ii. The face value of the Issue is not less than N10 billion.

iii. The market value of the mortgages securitizing the issued MBS shall not be lower than the ratio 1.3:1. Any shortfall in the value of the collateral can be made up by FGN Securities, with face value not exceeding 25% of the MBS.
iv. They are tradeable on a securities exchange registered by SEC.
v. The Promoters/Originators shall retain a minimum percentage of the Issue,
as determined by SEC Rules, which shall be maintained throughout the tenor of the issue.

vi. Make full disclosure of information on the MBS to investors, including corporate governance standards, annual valuation reports of the underlying pool of assets backing the securities, and any other information necessary for assessing inherent risks in each investment, including issues of title to land and properties.
6.2.5.2 Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT)
In the case of such REITs, the following requirements shall apply:
i. Meet the rating requirements in Section 6.1. However, where it is an Initial Public Offer, the Fund Manager shall have a minimum Investment Manager rating of 'BBB'.

ii. The Principal Officers of the Fund Manager, namely, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer, shall each have a minimum of 10 years of relevant investment management experience or relevant project management experience, five years of which shall have been in senior management positions.
iii. The face value of the issue is not less than N10 billion.
iv. The Prospectus shall specifically state that the securities shall subsequently be listed or have a memorandum listing on a registered or recognized Securities Exchange within a stipulated period.
v. The Promoters shall retain a minimum of 5% of the Fund, subject to SEC Rule, issued from time to time.

vi. Make full disclosure of information on the Fund to investors, including corporate governance standards, annual valuation reports of underlying assets and any information necessary for assessing inherent risks in each investment, including issues of title to land and properties.
6.2.6 Requirements for Asset-Backed Securities (ABS)
Pension Fund Assets can be invested in Asset-Backed Securities (ABS), provided the issuer and the securities meet the requirements stipulated below:
i. Compliance with the rating requirements in Section 6.1.
ii. The face value of the Issue is not less than N10 billion.

iii. The market value of the assets securitizing the issued ABS shall not be lower than the ratio 1.4:1. Any shortfall in the value of the collateral can be made up with FGN Securities, with face value not exceeding 25% of the ABS.
iv. They are tradeable on a securities exchange registered by the SEC.
v. The Promoters/Originators shall retain a minimum percentage of the Issue, as determined by SEC Rules, which shall be maintained throughout the tenor of the issue.

vi. Make full disclosure of information on the ABS to investors including corporate governance standards, annual valuation reports of the underlying pool of assets backing the securities, and any other information necessary for assessing inherent risks in each investment, including issues of title to land and properties.
vii. Any other additional conditions the Commission may stipulate from time to time.
6.2.7 Requirements for Ordinary Shares
Pension fund assets can only be invested in ordinary shares of public limited/private companies based on the following conditions:
i. The issuing companies' shares are listed and quoted on a securities exchange registered by the SEC or proposed to be listed and quoted through an IPO, listing by introduction or private placement.
ii. In the case of Private placement, securities shall certify the listing and disclosure and reporting requirements of the SEC.
iii. The Company has an operating track record of having made taxable profits for at least three out of the five years preceding the investment, and paid
dividends or issued bonus shares for at least one out of the five years.
iv. Pension Fund Assets in Fund I may be invested in the ordinary share of listed/unlisted companies with a one-year operating record, subject to the Commission's 'no objection'.

v. Pension fund investments may be made in a newly established quoted company that evolved as a result of merger, acquisition, or any other combination arrangement of existing corporate entities, subject to the condition that, at least, one of the erstwhile companies had satisfied the minimum quality requirements for investment in ordinary shares, stated in Section 6.2.8.1 (i) and (iii) above.
6.2.8 Requirements for Money Market Instruments
Pension Fund Assets can be invested in the money market instruments of banks and commercial paper of corporate entities, based on the following conditions:
i. The bank or corporate entity shall meet the rating requirements in Section 6.1.
ii. All Commercial papers and Bankers Acceptance shall comply with the CBN guidelines on the issuance of CPs and BAs.
iii. In the case of Bankers Acceptances (BAs) issued on behalf of a third party, they shall carry the full guarantee of the bank.

iv. Where the investment is in a Non-Interest Compliant money market instrument, it shall be in compliance with the CBN's guidelines for the regulation & supervision of institutions offering non-interest financial services.
v. Where the investment is in a Commercial Paper (CP), such CP shall be issued through a trading facility registered by the Securities and Exchange Commission and/or the Central Bank of Nigeria.
6.2.9 Requirements for Mutual Funds
Pension Fund Assets can be invested in the investment certificates of Open, Closed-End or Hybrid Investment Funds, including Indexed/Exchange Traded
Funds (ETFs), and similar Non-Interest compliant instruments, based on the following criteria:
i. The Fund is approved and registered by SEC.
ii. The minimum asset value for Open/ Close-ended/ Hybrid Investment Funds, including Exchange Traded Funds eligible for pension fund investment, shall be N10 billion.
iii. The Fund has a memorandum listing on a Securities Exchange registered by SEC.
iv. The Promoters shall retain a minimum percentage of the Fund, subject to SEC Rules. This shall, however, not apply to Open-end Funds.

v. The Principals managing the Funds, namely, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer, shall each have a minimum of 10 years relevant and continuous investment management experience, five years of which must have been in senior management positions.

vi. There are full disclosures of information on the Fund to investors, including investment and risk management strategies, corporate governance standards, yearly audited financial statements, among others.
6.2.9.2 Where it is an ETF:
i. The Sponsor and Fund Manager are recognized or registered with SEC.
ii. It shall be listed and trade-able on a Securities Exchange registered by SEC.
iii. The Fund Manager shall possess the relevant expertise to issue the ETF, as well as establish and maintain a secondary market for the issuance.
iv. The underlying Index, basket of securities or physical assets whose performance the ETF intends to track shall be clearly stated in the prospectus/offer document.
v. The underlying securities or assets of the ETF shall be held in a Custody arrangement or Depositary Account approved or recognized by SEC.
6.2.10 Requirements for Private Equity
Pension Fund Assets can be invested in Private Equity Funds subject to the following requirements:

i. The Fund shall have well-defined and publicized investment objectives and strategy, as well as disclosures of pricing of underlying assets; annual financial statements audited by independent firm(s) of chartered accountants registered by the Financial Reporting Council (FRC) ; and any other necessary information.

ii. The PE Fund Vehicle shall have satisfactory pre-defined liquidity/exit routes such as Initial Public Offers, Sale to industry buyers, and use of buy-out instruments in investing in the underlying companies or projects.
iii. The Funds shall be managed by experienced Fund Managers, versed in PE investments and registered with the SEC as Fund Managers.

iv. The key Principals of the Fund Manager must each have at least ten (10) years' experience in investment and management of third-party assets, or relevant project management experience in sectors of the economy in which the PE Fund shall invest, out of which five years must be PE investment experience.

v. The key Principals shall not exit the Fund without prior notice, of not less than 90 days, to the Commission through the PFA; and this 'exit clause' shall be expressly stated as a condition in the investment agreement/ covenant between the PFA and the Fund Manager.

vi. The key principals of the fund must have successfully exited at least one investment from the previous Fund. The key principals shall include the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer.

vii. Where a PE Fund does not have globally known Foundations & Endowments, MDFOs or Sovereign Wealth Funds (SWFs) as Limited Partners, but the Fund Manager has a minimum Investment Manager Rating of 'BBB', the Fund Manager shall retain a minimum investment of 3% of the PE Fund.

viii. However, where there are globally known Foundations & Endowments, MDFOs or SWFs as Limited Partners in the Fund or any other Pan-African /Multi-country PE Fund being managed by the Fund Manager, the Fund Manager shall retain a minimum investment of 1% of the PE Fund.

ix. Such globally known Foundations and Endowments, as stated in subsections (vi) and (vii) above, shall be in existence for a minimum of 10 years and have a fund size of not less than US$1 billion as confirmed from its audited annual financial statements.
x. A minimum of 30% of the Fund shall be invested in companies or projects within Nigeria or companies that generate up to 40% of their operating revenue in Nigeria.
xi. The Fund shall have an Advisory Board with representatives of Limited Partners being in the majority.

xii. PFAs are to ensure at all times that the above-mentioned Advisory Board has responsibility over audit functions regarding transactions with parties related to the Fund and the Fund's internal investment guidelines and policies.
6.2.10.2 Co-Investment of Pension Funds
PFAs may enter into Co-Investment arrangements for a specific transaction(s) following a PFA's investment in the main PE/Infrastructure Fund under the following conditions:

i. Co-Investment arrangements shall be made through Special Purpose CoInvestment Vehicles (SPCV). The SPCV shall be set up by the General Partner (GP) of the Fund with clearly defined legal status, rights and rules of the SPCV.

ii. The Governance Agreements under Co-Investment shall clearly delineate the roles and responsibilities of the GP and the investors in the CoInvestment arrangement. This includes governance rights, risk management, pre-emptive rights, liquidity and exit arrangements in the Co-
Investment arrangement.
iii. Co-Investment arrangements for pension fund investments shall not be on less favourable terms than the main fund.
iv. PFAs shall not be allowed to buy off the Co-Investment interest of other investors who may want to exit before maturity.
v. A PFA's exposure under any Co-Investment arrangement shall not exceed 50% of its investment in the main fund.
vi. A PFA's exposure under any Co-Investment arrangement shall form part of its global exposure and be subject to the maximum limits stipulated in this Regulation.
vii. All categories of fees under the Co-Investment arrangement shall be clearly defined in the Co-Investment Agreement.
viii. The Pension Fund shall not be liable for any cost or fee not stated in the CoInvestment Agreement.

ix. PFAs must ensure that relevant documentation required for the initial and ongoing due diligence is provided by the GP, including but not limited to board meeting minutes, human capital information and deal pipeline development to enable the PFA to undertake its due diligence.
x. Issues related to conflict of interest shall be in line with Section 7.0 of the Investment Regulation.
xi. Fund manager shall provide a quarterly valuation of pension fund investments under any Co-Investment arrangement, clearly stating the value of a PFA's investments.
xii. The valuation of pension assets deployed under a Co-Investment arrangement shall be based on quarterly valuations reported by the Fund Manager.
xiii. The Fund Manager shall also provide the valuation methodology alongside the valuations of pension fund investments under any Co-Investment arrangement.
Revised Regulation on Investment of Pension Fund Assets
xiv. Due to the additional risks involved in Co-Investment arrangements, PFAs shall ensure adequate due diligence before committing Pension Funds to Co-Investment arrangements.
xv. PFAs seeking to enter into a Co-Investment arrangement with an eligible Fund Manager shall obtain a "No Objection" from the Commission.
xvi. Co-Investment arrangement shall only be executed with a Fund whose key principals are, at least, on their second Fund.

xvii. The key principals of the fund must have successfully exited at least one investment from the previous Fund. The key principals shall include the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Investment Officer and any other applicable Principal Officer of the Fund.
xviii. PFAs shall ensure that all requirements for investments stipulated in this Regulation on Investment of Pension Fund Assets have been duly satisfied before any application for "No Objection".
6.2.11 Requirements for Securities Lending/Repurchase Agreement

PFAs/CPFAs can engage in Securities Lending arrangements and Repurchase Agreements (Reverse repos) on any exchange recognized and approved by the SEC or Central Bank of Nigeria to undertake such arrangements, provided:

i. The Lending/ Repo arrangement is done through a central counterparty/agent arrangement, where the central counterparty/agent stands in as a legal counterparty to the transaction and both parties provide all collateral required for the central counterparty/agent to provide a fullspectrum guarantee.
ii. The Central Counterparty/Agents are registered by the SEC to be counterparty/agents.
iii. The securities lending arrangement should be done in line with the Global Master Securities Lending Agreement (GMSLA).
iv. The Repo arrangement shall be done in line with the Nigerian Master Repurchase Agreement (NMRA) approved by the SEC.

v. All instruments involved in securities lending agreement shall be returned to the same fund at the conclusion of the lending arrangement. For fixed income securities, the assets involved shall be the assets held in the amortized cost bucket and shall also be returned to the same bucket at the conclusion of the lending arrangement.

Per-issue limits for PFAs and CPFAs engaging in securities lending arrangements or repo agreements shall be subject to a maximum of thirty percent (30%) of the PFA's or CPFA's holdings in any individual security, or such other limit as may be prescribed by the Commission from time to time through circulars or guidelines.
Notwithstanding 6.2.11.2, Securities Lending Arrangements and Repurchase Agreements (REPOs) shall be subject to Guidelines and Circulars issued by the Commission.
6.2.12 Requirements for Safekeeping Receipts
PFAs may invest in registered SKRs, provided that:
i. The SKR is approved by SEC.
ii. Listed and tradable on a SEC registered Exchange.
iii. The commodity shall be in the possession of a custodian registered by SEC.
iv. The transaction is carried out through a broker/dealing member registered by SEC.
v. The clearing/settlement of the receipt shall be done through a central security depository registered by SEC to undertake such transactions.
vi. The underlying commodity with the custodian shall be insured by a licensed insurer with a minimum credit rating of 'A'.
6.2.13 Requirements for Exchange Traded Derivatives
PFAs may engage in exchange-traded derivatives contract solely for the purpose of Risk Management, provided that:
i. The derivative is approved by SEC.
ii. It is listed and tradable on a SEC registered Exchange.
iii. The derivative is either Futures, Options, Forward Rate Agreement (FRA) or Swaps registered by SEC or counterparties licensed by the CBN with a minimum credit rating of 'A'.
iv. Swaps shall be solely for the purpose of hedging against foreign currency exposure.
v. For FRA, the PFA shall comply with the provisions of Section 7.1 of this Regulation.
vi. The clearing/settlement of the derivative shall be done through a central security depository registered by SEC or counterparties licensed by CBN to undertake such transactions.
vii. FRA and Swaps may be executed as bilateral (non-exchange negotiated) contracts.
viii. Notwithstanding (i-vi) above, Exchange Traded Derivatives shall be subject to guidelines and circulars issued by the Commission.
7.0 Conflict of Interest
PFAs or any of their agents are prohibited from investing Pension Fund Assets in the shares and/ or Securities Lending and Repurchase Agreement Arrangements by the following:
i. A Pension Fund Administrator.
ii. A Pension Fund Custodian.
iii. A Holding Company (HoldCo) of a Licensed Pension Fund Operator (LPFO) or any Subsidiary controlled by the Holding Company or Group.
iv. Related party/person of any shareholder of the PFA/PFC/HoldCo of PFA/PFC or any arrangement wherein the ultimate beneficiary is a related party of the PFA/PFC.
v. An employee of the PFA/PFC.
vi. The spouse or any relationship with persons referred to in (iv) to (v) of this
paragraph that can be reasonably construed as a related person.
Exception to Section 7.1 shall only be in the case of PFA's investment in money market instruments of an affiliate bank of the PFA or the PFC holding pension fund assets on its behalf.
The PFA or any of its agents shall not sell Pension Fund Assets to the following:
i. Itself.
ii. A Pension Fund Custodian.
iii. A Holding Company (HoldCo) of a Licensed Pension Fund Operator (LPFO) or any Subsidiary controlled by the Holding Company or Group.
iv. Any shareholder, director or related party/person of the PFA, or PFC holding pension fund assets on its behalf or HoldCo of which the PFA/PFC is a member.
v. Related party/person of any shareholder of the PFA.
vi. Any employee of the PFA.
vii. The spouse or any relationship with persons referred to in (iv) to (vi) of this paragraph that can be reasonably construed as a related person.
viii. The PFC holding Pension Fund Assets to the order of the PFA.
The PFA or any of its agents shall not:
i. Apply Pension Fund Assets under its management by way of loans and credits, or as collateral for any loan taken by any person.
ii. Divulge or utilize confidential information regarding pension fund investment decisions for any personal, corporate or related benefit.

A PFA shall transact not more than 30% of its total trades in equities (purchases and sales valued in Naira terms) in a calendar year, with broker firms that are related parties to the PFA, its Directors, and Shareholders.
Members of the Board, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer of PFAs shall disclose and abstain from taking investment decisions in which they have interest.

The Board Risk Management Committee shall develop a framework that would review Conflict of Interest issues and render quarterly reports to the Commission. The reports shall contain, amongst other necessary information, the nature of all conflict of interest issues and transactions concerning related persons within the period; values of such transactions; treatment of such issues/transactions; resolutions/ decisions taken; and follow-up actions, if any.
8.0 The Multi-Fund Structure
8.1 General Provisions
With respect to the multi-fund structure, the following shall apply:
i. The Multi-Fund Structure shall comprise seven funds, and all PFAs shall continue to offer the Multi-Fund Structure for the RSA Fund.

ii. The seven funds shall include Fund I, Fund II, Fund III, Fund IV (Retiree Fund), Fund V - Conservative (Micro Pension Fund), Fund V - Growth (Micro Pension Fund), Fund VI (Non-interest Fund), which shall be split into Fund VI Active and Fund VI Retiree Funds and Fund VII (Dollar Denominated Fund).
iii. The funds shall differ in their exposure to variable income instruments.

iv. The exposure to variable income instruments is defined as the sum of a PFA's investments in Ordinary Shares and participation units of Open Closed-ended, and Hybrid Funds; Real Estate Investment Trust; Infrastructure Funds; and Private Equity Funds comprising its current holdings and any future financial commitments to the acquisition of participation units in these Funds.
v. In line with (iv) above, the maximum exposure to variable income instruments by the Fund Types are as follows:
Fund I: 95% of Portfolio Value
Fund II: 75% of Portfolio Value
Fund III: 20% of Portfolio Value
Fund IV: 10% of Portfolio Value
Fund V - Conservative: 5% of Portfolio Value
Fund V - Growth: 45% of Portfolio Value
Fund VI (Active): 75% of Portfolio Value
Fund VI (Retiree):10% of Portfolio Value
Fund VII (Dollar-denominated fund): 30% of Portfolio Value

vi. PFAs are also expected to invest in such a way as to clearly delineate the actual exposure to variable income instruments in Funds I, II and III. For example, the exposure to variable income instruments in Fund I should be higher than the exposure in Fund II. Likewise, the exposure in Fund II shall be higher than the exposure in Fund III.
8.2 Default Mechanism
Effective from the date of implementation of the Multi-Fund Structure, the PFAs shall allocate contributors to various Fund Types according to the following criteria:
i. Membership of Fund I shall strictly be by formal request by a Contributor who is 49 years and below as at his/her last birthday.
ii. Active Contributors who are 49 years and below as at their last birthdays shall be assigned to Fund II.
iii. Active Contributors who are 50 years and above as at their last birthdays shall be assigned to Fund III.
iv. Fund IV and VI shall strictly be for RSA retirees only.
v. Fund V shall strictly be for contributors under the Micro-pension Scheme.
vi. Fund VI shall be for contributors and retirees' who choose to have their contributions invested in Non-interest Money and Capital Market Products.
vii. Fund VII shall be for contributors who are Nigerians living abroad and

individuals in Nigeria, whether Nigerian or foreign, who work for foreign companies or international organizations, receive all or part of their income in foreign currency, and are not subject to Section 2(2) of the PRA 2014.
8. 3 Active Choices

Subsequent to the implementation of the Multi-Fund Structure, contributors in the formal sector are allowed to choose the Type of Fund in which they desire to be, subject to the restrictions of Fund IV and VI (Retiree Fund). Furthermore, for Fund V, contributors have the option of choosing between Fund V - Conservative and Fund V - Growth at inception. Notwithstanding, the following rules shall apply:
i. An active Contributor in Fund II who wishes to be assigned to Fund I shall make a formal request to the PFA.
ii. An active Contributor in Fund III who wishes to be assigned to Fund II shall make a formal request to the PFA.
iii. An RSA Retiree or active Contributor who is 50 years and above shall not be allowed to choose Fund I.
iv. An active contributor in Fund I, II or III who wishes to move to Fund VI Active shall make a formal request to the PFA.
v. A retiree in Fund IV who wishes to move to Fund VI Retiree shall make a formal request to the PFA.
vi. A contributor in Fund V - Conservative or Fund V - Growth who wishes to switch between the two shall be required to submit a formal request to the PFA.
8.4 Transfers between Fund Types within a PFA
An active Contributor may, subject to a formal application made to the PFA, switch from one Fund Type to another Fund Type within a given PFA, twice in 12 months, without paying any fees.

Any additional requests for switches among Funds within a PFA by the active Contributor shall attract a fee of an amount not less than a minimum value, to be determined by the Commission from time to time.
8.5 Fund Types
8.5.1 RSA Funds (I-IV)

The Multi-Fund Structure shall comprise Fund I, Fund II, Fund III, and Fund IV (Retiree Fund). Funds I, II, III and IV shall differ among themselves according to their overall exposure to variable income instruments.
8.5.2 Fund V (Micro Pension Fund)
Fund V shall be designated for contributors under the Micro Pension Scheme and divided into two categories: a Conservative Fund (Fund V - Conservative) and a Growth Fund (Fund V - Growth).

The Investment of the Fund shall be undertaken in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation. The contributions shall, by default, be allocated as follows: 60% retained for pensions and 40% available for contingent withdrawals, or such other allocation ratio as may be determined by the Commission from time to time through circulars or guidelines.
8.5.3 Fund VI (Non-interest Fund)
Fund VI shall be for contributors who choose to have their pension contributions invested in Non-Interest Money and Capital Market Products.
Fund VI shall be separated into two funds for Active RSA holders and Retirees as follows:
i. Active Non-Interest Fund (Active Fund VI): For contributors in Funds I, II and III who have elected to move their contributions to Fund VI.
ii. Retiree Non-Interest Fund (Retiree Fund VI): For Retirees in Fund IV who move their contributions to Retiree Fund VI.
Ethical Principles: The following ethical principles shall apply:
i. Fund VI assets shall not be invested in the production or trading of alcohol, pornography, weaponry, gambling/betting, speculation, interest earning
ventures and other ventures of similar nature contrary to Shari'ah principles and as may be determined by FRACE from time to time.
ii. Fund VI shall be based on the principles of Wakala Bil-Istithmar (investment agency contract) with the PFA acting as the investment agent for active RSA contributors in Fund VI.
iii. The principle of Mudarabah contract (profit-sharing and loss-bearing partnership) shall be used for retirees in Fund IV who opted for Fund VI.

iv. Fund VI assets are to be invested in instruments that are free from speculation and uncertainty that might lead to destruction or loss, otherwise known as 'Gharar' under Islamic commercial jurisprudence.

v. Pursuant to (i) above, the fundamental value of a security with respect to the annual income it may bring such as dividends, is to be considered by PFAs before future price considerations. Derivative products such as Futures Contracts, Swaps, Options and Forwards are considered as speculative and uncertain.

vi. PFAs shall obtain sufficient knowledge (number of units, terms of the sale/contract, and monetary worth) of the instrument(s) intended to be exchanged before taking investment decisions on Fund VI assets.
8.5.3.4 Eligibility Requirements
i. RSA holders in Fund I, Fund II and Fund III are eligible to move their RSA contributions to Fund VI (Active Fund VI).
ii. Retirees in Fund IV are eligible to move their RSA contributions to Fund VI (Retiree Fund VI).
iii. RSA contributors in Fund III can move their contributions directly to Retiree Fund VI at the time of retirement.
iv. The Commission shall determine the participation of Micro Pension Contributors in due course.
8.5.3.5 Allowable Instruments
i. The provisions of Section 5 of this regulation shall apply to Fund VI in respect of allowable instruments.
ii. Pursuant to (i) above, Fund VI assets shall be invested in the following instruments:
Government Sukuk, (including Islamic Treasury Bills and Euro Sukuk) issued by FGN, CBN or FGN Agencies and Infrastructure Sukuk, backed by FGN/CBN guarantee.
Corporate Sukuk (including Shari'ah compliant ABS, MBS, DNs, Euro Sukuk & Infrastructures Sukuk).
Supranational Sukuk.
Shari'ah-compliant Money Market instruments.
Shari'ah-compliant ordinary shares (including DRs).
Shari'ah-compliant infrastructure funds.
Shari'ah-compliant private equity Funds.
Shari'ah-compliant Open/Closed/Hybrid Funds.
Shari'ah-compliant real Estate funds.
Shari'ah-compliant Safekeeping receipts.

iii. Fund VI assets are also allowed to be invested in conventional assets where a PFA is unable to find approved Non-Interest instruments. The conventional assets are to be phased out as more approved Non-Interest instruments become available.

iv. The conventional assets shall comply with the provisions in 8.5.3.3 above. However, the conventional securities to augment Shari'ah-compliant assets could be interest-bearing but should not be in sectors/businesses whose underlying assets/products do not meet the basic ethical principles as stated in 8.5.3.3 above.
8.5.3.6 Quality of Instruments/Securities
i. The ethical principles specified in Section 8.5.3.3 above shall apply to Fund VI in respect to the quality requirements for instruments to be invested in the Fund.
ii. The rating requirements with respect to selection of counter parties and investment instruments in Fund VI shall be in line with the provisions of Section 6.1 of this regulation.
8.5.3.7 Portfolio Structure

i. The Portfolio composition of Fund VI shall in the first instance, be made up of Shari'ah-compliant instruments, and any gap shall be filled with conventional securities/instruments that meet the quality requirements specified in section 8.2.3.3 of this regulation.

ii. Licensed PFAs shall in addition to other statutory returns, render monthly and quarterly reports to the Commission, providing justifications for all nonShari'ah-compliant securities in the Fund VI portfolio.

iii. The Portfolio Mix (compliant vs non-compliant) in Fund VI shall be progressively phased out in favour of Shari'ah-compliant securities. The progressive phasing of investment in favour of Shari'ah-compliant investment shall be reported quarterly to the Pension Industry Non-interest Advisory Committee (PINAC) by the Commission for proper monitoring of compliance with Shari'ah principles. The report should contain a percentage split between compliant and non-compliant instruments.

iv. The Commission shall, pursuant to review of the market situation and availability of products, determine the terminal date for conventional assets in Fund VI, after which Fund VI shall fully comprise of only certified Shari'ahcompliant products.
8.5.3.8 Governance Structure

i. There shall be a Pension Industry Non-interest Advisory Committee (PINAC) established for the Pension Industry to provide guidance and/or advice on the application of Shari'ah standards on matters relating to investments of
Fund VI assets and ensure continuous Shari'ah audit and purification of the Investment Pool of Fund VI assets, amongst other functions.
ii. The PINAC shall serve as an advisory body to the Commission on Islamic Finance matters and specifically on all subsidiary legislations on investment of Fund VI assets.

iii. The Commission shall seek the advice of the PINAC on matters relating to Islamic commercial jurisprudence. The advice of PINAC in this regard shall be used by the Commission as an input into its regulatory decisions on the management of Fund VI by PFAs.
8.5.4 Fund VII (Dollar Denominated Fund)
Eligibility Criteria: Fund VII shall be for the following class of contributors/arrangement:

i. Contributors who are Nigerians living abroad and individuals in Nigeria, whether Nigerian or foreign, who work for foreign companies or international organizations, receive all or part of their income in foreign currency, and are not subject to Section 2(2) of the PRA 2014.
ii. Corporate entities operating in Nigeria, with demonstrated foreign currency revenue earnings, may elect to set up Additional Benefit Schemes for their employees.
8.5.4.2. General Investment Principles

i. Foreign currency pension contributions shall be invested in line with the PRA 2014 and Regulations and Guidelines issued by the Commission to ensure safety and fair returns. The Board of Directors of the PFA shall approve the investment policy of the foreign currency fund.
ii. The General Principles under Section 2.0 of this Regulation shall also apply to the investment of foreign currency contributions.
iii. PFAs shall invest foreign currency contributions within Nigeria in line with allowable investments set out by relevant provisions in this Regulation.

iv. In line with Section 1.50 of this Regulation, the Board Investment Strategy Committee of the PFA shall formulate the internal investment strategies for investments in the foreign currency fund, which the Board shall approve.
v. Investments of foreign currency contributions shall be executed and retained in foreign currency (USD).

vi. Notwithstanding the provisions of subparagraph (v) above, PFAs may invest foreign currency contributions in eligible Naira-denominated instruments only where an effective currency hedge is arranged and in place prior to execution of the investment transaction. Such hedging shall be maintained at all times for the duration of the investment, in accordance with the PRA, 2014 (as amended) and any guidelines issued by the Commission.

8.5.4.3 Allowable Investment Instruments
Investments may include:

i. Foreign currency-denominated bonds, Euro bonds, DRs/Ns and other securities issued by the Federal Government of Nigeria, CBN, their agencies, and companies, provided that the Federal Government or the CBN guarantees such securities.
ii. Money market instruments of eligible Deposit Money Banks (in line with this Regulation).

iii. Eurobonds and foreign bonds issued by eligible listed and unlisted Nigerian corporate entities. The bonds shall be listed on a security exchange that is a member of the World Federation of Exchanges.
iv. Supranational bonds issued by MDFOs approved by the FMOF and Sukuk issued by eligible Deposit Money Banks.
v. DNs/Rs as stipulated in Section 6.2.2 of this Regulation.
vi. Non-interest investment Funds and Mutual funds, index funds or ETFs with underlying investments in equities, bonds, commodities, real estate, money market instruments or a blended fund.
vii. Specialist funds registered with the SEC, such as REITs, Private Equity Funds and Infrastructure Funds.
9.0 Investment Limit

A PFA may invest the pension fund assets of any one Fund in the ordinary share of an unlisted company in line with the provisions of Section 5.5 of this Regulation. However, this is subject to a maximum limit of 3% of the issued share capital.

blocks.x: 10.0 Violations of Investment Limits

Limits imposed by this Regulation may be temporarily violated in cases of assets revaluation. However, where such violation results from market appreciation in the value of securities, the PFA shall immediately notify the Commission and make no further purchases of such security until the portfolio is rebalanced.

If at any time a PFA willfully violates any of the investment limits so prescribed in Section 9.0 of this Regulation, the PFA may maintain the investments but shall not make any additional investments in that instrument until there is rebalancing. The rebalancing shall be done within thirty (30) days from the day of violation. Where there is a loss as a result of the violation, the PFA shall refund the loss to the Fund. In addition, the PFA shall pay a penalty for violation of the approved limit, as may be determined by the Commission.

If a bank fails to fulfill the rating requirements stated in this Regulation, the PFA shall divest itself of all money market instruments issued by the bank within the following 3 months, while Commercial papers issued by both banks and other corporate entities may be held till maturity.

12.0 Voting Rights
PFAs shall instruct PFCs to exercise all voting rights attached to Pension Fund Assets in a manner that is prudent, diligent, and in the best long-term interests of Contributors and Beneficiaries.
Each PFA shall maintain a Board-approved Voting and Engagement Policy, which shall:
a. Set out the principles and guidelines for exercising voting rights;
b. Provide for escalation and engagement processes with investee companies;
c. Include measures for identifying, managing, and disclosing conflicts of interest;
d. Specify procedures for recalling lent securities to vote on material matters; and
e. Outline oversight and evaluation of the PFCs.
PFCs shall record, retain and report details of all votes cast on behalf of the PFAs/CPFAs.
PFAs/CPFAs shall retain details of all proxy votes cast by the PFCs, including the rationale for significant votes, and provide the Commission with such records upon
request.
PFAs shall disclose annually to Contributors and the Commission a summary of significant votes, engagements, and outcomes achieved.
PFCs shall, upon the instruction of PFAs/CPFAs, execute votes in a timely and accurate manner, and maintain appropriate evidence of such actions for regulatory verification.
13.0 Closed Pension Funds and Approved Existing Schemes

Pursuant to Section 50 (1) (f) of the PRA 2014, all investments made prior to the commencement of the Act in assets which are contrary to Section 86 of the Act, may be maintained by entities whose existing schemes have been approved by the Commission to continue to exist. This is, however, subject to appropriate Guidelines that may be issued by the Commission.

CPFAs and Approved Existing Schemes (AESs) may continue to invest in approved asset classes and securities (including real estate properties and foreign investments) provided that they do not exceed the investment limits specified in their Internal Investment Guidelines as approved by the Commission.
In line with 13.2 above, the investment limits in the Internal Investment Guidelines shall be set by the Trustees of the Fund.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 13.2 above, CPFAs/AESs shall not convert Naira into foreign currencies for investments outside Nigeria, without compliance with Section 87(2) of PRA 2014 and Guidelines for Investment in Foreign Currency Dominated Assets to be issued by the Commission from time to time.

Where a Closed Pension Fund Administrator or Approved Existing Scheme had invested up to the investment limit prescribed for that asset class in its Internal Investment Guidelines, it may only make new investments in that asset class if there is portfolio growth to accommodate the additional investments.

CPFAs and Approved Existing Schemes may directly invest in real estate properties, subject to their Internal Investment Guidelines and the Guidelines on Direct Real Estate Investments issued by the Commission.

CPFAs and Approved Existing Schemes operating defined contribution schemes may maintain separate Funds for Existing and Retired employees, which should be reflected in the Internal Investment Guidelines approved by the Commission.
Any amendment(s) to the Internal Investment Guidelines of a CPFA/Approved Existing Scheme shall have the Commission's prior approval before implementation.
14.0 Reviews
This Regulation is subject to periodic reviews by the Commission.
Notwithstanding the above provision, the Commission may from time to time, issue circulars to the provisions of this Regulation based on prevailing market developments and/or emerging issues.
